messages.author: cd016d159ac3dc3c
messages.subject: Warning Messages 1: In sqrt(1/diag(V)) : NaNs produced 2: In cov2cor(OUT[[b]]) :
parts:
Hi, 

I'm not sure what these warning messages mean and I've encountered them once before (see previous email "Warning messages: 1: In sqrt(1/diag(V)) 2: cov2cor(OUT[[b]])") . 

What do they mean? Can I interpret my results? 

Attached is the LDSC data and code for my bifactor model (where I added residual correlations between AUD and OCD to improve model fit) to reproduce the error. 

Thank you! 

Camille 

LDSCoutput <- readRDS("ldsc.rds")

GWISmodel <- 'Internalizing =~  Neff_Meta_Dep + Neff_Meta_PTSD + Neff_Meta_OCD  + Neff_Meta_SH + Neff_Meta_Eat_Rev + Neff_Meta_ANX
                   Thought_Disorder =~ a*Neff_Meta_SCZ + a*Neff_Meta_BPD
                   Externalizing =~ b*Other.Substance.Hazard.Dependence_Neff + b*Neff_Meta_AUD

                   P =~  Neff_Meta_Dep + Neff_Meta_PTSD  + Neff_Meta_SH + Neff_Meta_Eat_Rev + Neff_Meta_OCD+
                   Neff_Meta_ANX + Neff_Meta_SCZ+ Neff_Meta_BPD + Other.Substance.Hazard.Dependence_Neff + Neff_Meta_AUD
                 
                  Internalizing ~~ 0*Thought_Disorder
                  Externalizing ~~ 0*Internalizing
                  Thought_Disorder ~~ 0*Externalizing
                 
                   P ~~ 0*Thought_Disorder
                   P ~~ 0*Internalizing
                   P ~~ 0*Externalizing
                   
                   Neff_Meta_OCD ~~ Neff_Meta_AUD

                  Neff_Meta_Dep ~~ c*Neff_Meta_Dep
                  c > 0.000001 '


GWISoutput<-usermodel(covstruc = LDSCoutput, estimation = "DWLS",
                      model = GWISmodel, CFIcalc = TRUE,
                      imp_cov = T)

GWISoutput

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Warning Messages 1: In sqrt(1/diag(V)) : NaNs produced 2: In cov2cor(OUT[[b]]) :
parts:
Hi Camille, 

That warning is popping up in this case because of the constraint you are having to put on the residual variance in depression to keep it above 0 (warning goes away when you remove the constraint). The way I think about this situation is the warning is cueing you into an issue with the estimates resulting from the constraint and so the question is how much results shift with and without the constraint in the model. I would say a quick look at the standardized factor loadings in the model with and without the constraint indicates that results do shift quite a bit and so I would lean towards not trusting these model results. 

I also typically like to use unit variance identification when working with two-indicator latents as the loadings are otherwise both fixed to 1 with the equality constraint. When I tried that out the models were failing to converge, which to my mind further indicates some instability in this model specification. 

It already looks like you've done some careful modeling here with the residual covariance included, the orthogonal relationships among the three factors specified, equality constraints in the model, and constraints on the negative residual. All that to say I imagine it may be difficult to troubleshoot this model too much more as it seems like you've already done a lot of that work. Possible issues that stand out here are that there are two, two-indicator latents, that would be good to get a third indicator for if possible (of course two-indicator latents are fine it just may be causing convergence issues here) and the bifactor p-factor soaking up additional variance on top of everything else that is pushing something like MDD, that already has a really high rg of .9 with ANX, to have a negative residual. You could consider a hierarchical specification of p as an alternative, consider bringing in other variables, or try alternative specifications of this bifactor model. 

Best, 
 Andrew
